```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  fig.width = 7,
  fig.height = 4.5

```

```{r setup}
library(multisiteDGP)
```

Simulated data usually go on to a model. `as_metafor()` and `as_baggr()`
return a simulated data set under the column names that metafor and baggr
expect. The sections below show what each function returns, fit a
random-effects model with metafor, and compare the fit with the truth.

The examples use the data set from `vignette("multisiteDGP")`. Its design has
a grand mean `tau` of 0 and a cross-site standard deviation `sigma_tau` of
0.2.

```{r data}
dat <- sim_multisite(preset_education_modest(), seed = 1)
print(dat, n = 4)
```

## metafor

`as_metafor()` returns three columns. `yi` is the estimate, `vi` its sampling
variance, and `sei` its standard error. Both functions only rename columns,
so they run whether or not the other packages are installed.

```{r metafor}
mf <- as_metafor(dat)
print(mf, n = 4)
```

Row 4 holds the estimate (0.410), the sampling variance (0.333), and the
standard error (0.577) of site 4. `metafor::rma()` fits a random-effects model
to the estimates and their sampling variances.

```{r rma, eval = requireNamespace("metafor", quietly = TRUE)}
fit <- metafor::rma(yi, vi, data = mf)
fit
```

Under `Model Results`, `estimate` is the estimated grand mean, $-0.0331$. Its
95 percent interval, from $-0.1230$ to 0.0568, contains the design value of 0.
In metafor's output, `tau` is not the grand mean but the cross-site standard
deviation, which multisiteDGP calls `sigma_tau`. The fit estimates it at
0.1419. The design value is 0.2, and the 50 simulated site effects have a
standard deviation of 0.166 (the `sigma_tau` line of the header).

`as_metafor()` leaves out the true site effects. Its rows are in the order
of `dat`, so `dat$tau_j` can be compared with whatever the model returns for
each site. `metafor::blup()` returns empirical-Bayes estimates of the site
effects.

```{r truth, eval = requireNamespace("metafor", quietly = TRUE)}
eb <- metafor::blup(fit)$pred
rmse <- function(x) sqrt(mean((x - dat$tau_j)^2))
round(c(observed = rmse(mf$yi), empirical_bayes = rmse(eb)), 3)
```

Against the true site effects, the root mean squared error is 0.277 for the
observed estimates and 0.153 for the empirical-Bayes estimates.

## baggr

`as_baggr()` returns the estimate and its standard error under the names `tau`
and `se`, which baggr expects for summary data.

```{r baggr}
bg <- as_baggr(dat)
print(bg, n = 4)
```

As a column of baggr's input, `tau` is the estimate of a site, which
multisiteDGP calls `tau_j_hat`. With `include_truth = TRUE`, the result has a
third column, `tau_true`, with the true site effects, for comparison with the
site estimates of the fitted model. The fit itself ignores that column.

```{r baggr-truth}
names(as_baggr(dat, include_truth = TRUE))
```

`baggr::baggr()` fits the same normal hierarchical model as `metafor::rma()`,
with prior distributions on the grand mean and the cross-site standard
deviation. In baggr this is the Rubin model. The call is shown without output
because it draws posterior samples with Stan.

```{r baggr-fit, eval = FALSE}
fit_baggr <- baggr::baggr(bg, model = "rubin")
fit_baggr
```

The printed fit reports a hypermean `tau` and a hyper-SD `sigma_tau`. These
are the grand mean and the cross-site standard deviation, under the names that
multisiteDGP uses.

## The returned columns

| Simulated data | `as_metafor()` | `as_baggr()` |
|---------------|---------------|-------------------|
| `tau_j` | | `tau_true` (optional) |
| `tau_j_hat` | `yi` | `tau` |
| `se_j` | `sei` | `se` |
| `se2_j` | `vi` | |

Both functions return a plain tibble with one row per site, in the order of
the simulated data, and copy the values without change. The `design` and
`diagnostics` attributes and the columns `site_index`, `z_j`, and `n_j` are
not carried over. If the design has covariates, their columns follow the
renamed ones. Data from `sim_meta()`, which have no site sizes, convert in
the same way.
